Subject: Orion Labs pilot — initial sizing ask

Team —

Quick context: Orion Labs (contact: Anna Lopez) is evaluating a Dedicated pilot with a committed slab. They expect production-like traffic during pilot days and want firm guidance on tokens/sec sizing, p95 latency fit for their SLA, and how much compute cushion we should recommend before asking them to commit.

Customer notes from discovery: average request token length ~ 240 (prompt+response), bursty pattern aligned to business hours in US-PST, projected peak concurrent requests 18–22 req/s for initial month. Their target SLO is p95 generation latency <= 600ms for typical 240-token responses (they accept higher tail for very long responses).

Key asks from sales:
- A short modeling doc that converts their req/s -> tokens/sec -> GPUs required for candidate model variants (13B and 7B quantized variants).
- Recommended headroom policy (x1.5/x2) and what that means in committed GPUs.
- Fallback plan: when to autoscale/fallback to smaller model or allow degraded latency.

Ben / Marissa, can you own the ROI/ops calc? Karthik, I need a short note on model performance assumptions (tokens/sec per GPU, latency envelope, impact of batching + prefix caching).

Deliverable by EOD Tuesday (2028-06-20) is ideal — we have an internal exec sync on Wednesday where we want a recommended ask to present. I attached a blank template (mutual_action_plan_draft.pdf) — please populate numbers and attach the spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Thu, Jun 18, 2028 at 10:21 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick context: Orion Labs (contact: Anna Lopez) is evaluating a Dedicated pilot with a committed slab. ...

Thanks Vivek — I put together a first-pass spreadsheet (orn-throughput-model-v1.xlsx) with two candidate model variants and the math we like to use for commitment sizing. High-level summary below; details are in the attachment.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Customer peak concurrent requests: 22 req/s
- Avg request tokens (prompt+response): 240 tokens
- Derived peak tokens/sec = 22 * 240 = 5,280 tokens/sec
- Latency SLO target p95 <= 600ms for these requests (as Vivek noted)

Model performance (baseline numbers):
- 13B quantized (int8, optimized kernels): ~3,500 tokens/sec sustained per A100-equivalent GPU for short sequences (<=512) with batching. p95 generation latency at 2k tokens/sec on a single GPU ~ 420ms (model-only).
- 7B quantized (int8): ~8,500 tokens/sec per GPU, p95 model-only latency ~ 210ms under moderate batching.

Sizing math:
- Required tokens/sec: 5,280.
- If we pick 13B: GPUs_needed_raw = ceil(5,280 / 3,500) = 2 GPUs -> delivered capacity ~7,000 tps (headroom ~1.33x).
- If we pick 7B: GPUs_needed_raw = ceil(5,280 / 8,500) = 1 GPU -> delivered capacity ~8,500 tps (headroom ~1.6x).

Headroom recommendation (ops + commercial risk):
- Minimum recommend: 1.5x headroom on committed slab (operational cushion for bursts and kernel stalls).
- Conservative recommend for SLA-backed customers: 2x headroom.

Implication: to hit 1.5x headroom for 13B we'd want 3 GPUs (3*3,500=10,500 tps -> ~2.0x headroom for the 5,280 baseline). For 7B that would stay at 1 GPU (8,500 -> ~1.6x) but the functional tradeoff is lower quality/decreased instruction-following vs 13B.

Operational notes:
- Prefix/KV caching on repeated sessions should reduce effective compute by ~12–18% for Orion's workload (they have many short conversational sessions), which improves effective headroom.
- Batching helps, but increases p95 — we should simulate burst tails.
- We recommend an autoscale policy that allows +1 burst GPU on top of committed slab for extreme short spikes with a short warmup window.

I attached the spreadsheet with worksheets: raw math, headroom scenarios, and a latency-tail plot. Please review and Karthik if you can add kernel-level caveats.

- Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer

On Fri, Jun 19, 2028 at 09:08 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Vivek — I put together a first-pass spreadsheet...

Couple of kernel/perf caveats to add into the sheet and the recommended playbook:

Model kernel throughput notes (empirical):
- 13B int8 (FP16 fallback for certain ops) on A100-p4/80GB-equivalent: 3.0k–3.8k tokens/sec depending on seq length and beam settings; at sequence length 240 we see ~3.5k as Ben used — that's a reasonable baseline.
- 7B int8 is fast (~7.5k–9k tps), but checkout and quantization quality varies by instruction set. Not always a drop-in for parity with 13B for instruction-heavy prompts.

Latency tail and batching tradeoffs:
- For p95 <=600ms target we should prefer lower batching depth for on-demand requests; batching window 5–10ms gives better latency but reduces throughput density.
- KV / prefix cache: warm sessions can reduce compute by ~15% on average but can create uneven request distribution (hot shards). Plan for shard-level headroom.

Headroom policy (operational):
- Recommended committed slab: choose model variant first (we recommend starting with 13B for quality).
- Commit 3 GPUs for 13B to achieve comfortable cushion (~3*3.5k=10.5k tps -> ~2x for baseline peak).
- Configure autoscale to allow +2 GPUs for bursts and a fallback route to 7B variant with rate-limited outputs if latency > 1s or queue depth grows.

Risk notes for commercial:
- If Orion demands contractual p95 at 600ms with financial penalties, consider requiring a higher commit (4 GPUs) or contractual exception for tail behavior.

I'll add these rows into the spreadsheet and label the cells with the kernel variance (low/median/high) so legal/sales can see the assumptions.

-Karthik
Staff Performance Engineer, Inference

Hi Vivek / Ben —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the spreadsheet — reviewed by our infra and product leads. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock a commit:

1) Our numbers are a bit burstier than the initial estimate — peak sawtooth within hour windows has produced short spikes up to 30 req/s (we reported average 22 earlier). Can you show the 30 req/s column in the sheet?
2) We prefer 13B quality but would like a fallback that does not double our p95 beyond 1s. If you propose a fallback to 7B, can you show expected p95 under that fallback?
3) Procurement question: we need a conservative committed proposal for the contract. If we sign a 3 GPU commit (per your recommendation), what is the expected sustained p95 assuming the 30 req/s spikes and 15% effective compute reduction from caching?

If you can reply with the 30req/s scenario and a short plain-English summary we can share with procurement, that will unblock an SOW draft.

Best,
Anna Lopez

On Wed, Jun 22, 2028 at 18:12 Anna Lopez <anna@orionlabs.com> wrote:

>

Anna — thanks for the clarity. I updated the spreadsheet (orn-throughput-model-v1.xlsx) and attached a one-page summary in the mutual_action_plan_draft.pdf. Short answers below so procurement has a crisp statement:

30 req/s scenario math (conservative):
- Peak requests: 30 req/s * 240 tokens/request = 7,200 tokens/sec gross.
- Apply conservative cache reduction 15% -> effective tokens/sec demand = 7,200 * 0.85 = 6,120 tps.

Committed slab outcomes (13B baseline, per-GPU = 3,500 tps median):
- 3 GPUs -> capacity = 3 * 3,500 = 10,500 tps -> effective headroom vs 6,120 tps = ~1.72x.
- Estimated p95 (model-only) at sustained 6,120 tps across 3 GPUs: ~520ms model-only. Add the network + router + JSON postprocessing envelope (~40–80ms typical) -> end-to-end p95 estimate = ~560–600ms.

Fallback to 7B (single GPU) during extreme pressure:
- 7B with quantization ~8,500 tps per GPU. If routed to 7B the p95 model-only at equivalent load is ~280–400ms depending on batching; end-to-end p95 estimate = ~320–480ms. Note: quality/perplexity tradeoffs vs 13B may impact evaluation metrics.

Recommendation for SOW language we can provide to procurement (one-liner):
- "Redwood will provision a committed slab of 3 A100-equivalent GPUs (13B quantized baseline) delivering ~10.5k tps gross capacity with an expected end-to-end p95 generation latency <= 600ms under the documented workload profile; an automated fallback route to a 7B quantized variant will be configured for extreme load events. Detailed performance assumptions and thresholds are documented in the attached spreadsheet."

Next steps: Vivek / Ben — I suggest we propose the 3 GPU commit in the SOW with a 30-day SLA exception window while we run an initial pilot and collect latency tails; we can renegotiate prior to a longer-term annual commit. I linked the HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ORN-2028-004) and the spreadsheet in the related_links.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
